A.note: Ruined quarter rendered as a monochrome tan sand-and-cardboard mass. Ruins are thin extruded wall slabs, and the rubble reads as grey umbrellas or cones. Troops are a tiny cluster at the bottom edge and unreadable. The right half is empty sand with only blurry shadows. There is no sky or smoke, and the lighting is flat.

B.note: Nearly identical to A. The ruin walls are slightly denser and the beams cast marginally stronger shadows. Troops are still a few red pixels. The same empty right half and umbrella-shaped rubble remain. The difference is negligible.

C.note: Only version with sky, horizon hills, sea, a bastioned sea wall, a bell tower, gardens and a fort on the ridge. Dense terracotta roofs give a convincing Mediterranean old town. The buildings are uniform boxes with matching windows and tiled-grid ground, so they look like a game or city-builder. There are no ships, smoke or visible damage, so the bombardment story is missing. The troops are two or three red specks.

why: C is the only frame with real depth, sky, harbour and an intact-town read, while A and B are near-identical, empty, monochrome ruin fields with umbrella-like rubble and no readable troops.
top_fix_for_best: Add scale and story. Place visible ships (ships of the line or frigates, with sails and flags) in the bay. Add drifting smoke plumes and a few ruined or burning buildings. Add a readable troop column in the streets. Break up the box-and-roof repetition with varied heights, chimneys and roof types. Replace the tiled ground with rough streets and add atmospheric haze for depth.
